input.question: What happens if you freeze a super strong container full of water?
input.ground_truth: There are different types of “ice” depending on pressure. Typical ice is ice-I; when freezing water under sufficient pressure, different types all the way to ice-XVI have been produced, some are unstable and can’t be found in nature. Most of these are more dense than water (ie the water would shrink rather than expand). It is hypothesized that under sufficient pressure (e.g. a strong enough container shrinking in size) water would freeze into a metallic form of ice.

Question: What happens if you freeze a super strong container full of water?

response.prediction:
Okay! Imagine you have a really, really strong box. You fill it with water and put it in the freezer. When you freeze the water, it turns into ice. But ice gets really, really big when it freezes, and it can break weak things.

If the box is super strong, the ice will get bigger inside, but the box will not break. But if the box isn’t strong enough, the ice might break it because ice takes up more space than water.

So, if you use a super strong container, the ice will just stay inside and nothing will break! But the water will turn into a big block of ice.
